title: Basic Data Types
code:
# Basic data types in R
numeric_var <- 42
character_var <- "Hello, R!"
logical_var <- TRUE
vector_var <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)

# Print variables
print(numeric_var)
print(character_var)
print(logical_var)
print(vector_var)

title: Data Frame Operations
code:
# Creating a data frame
df <- data.frame(
  name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"),
  age = c(25, 30, 35),
  salary = c(50000, 60000, 70000)
)

# Display the data frame
print(df)

# Access columns
print(df$name)
print(df["age"])

# Filter data
high_earners <- df[df$salary > 55000, ]
print(high_earners)

title: Statistical Functions
code:
# Generate random data
set.seed(123)
data <- rnorm(100, mean = 50, sd = 10)

# Basic statistics
mean_val <- mean(data)
median_val <- median(data)
sd_val <- sd(data)

# Print results
cat("Mean:", mean_val, "\n")
cat("Median:", median_val, "\n")
cat("Standard Deviation:", sd_val, "\n")

# Create a histogram
hist(data, main = "Normal Distribution", xlab = "Values")

title: Functions and Loops
Data Visualization with Base R
code:
# Sample data
x <- 1:10
y <- x^2 + rnorm(10, 0, 5)

# Create plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))  # 2x2 plot layout

# Scatter plot
plot(x, y, main = "Scatter Plot", xlab = "X values", ylab = "Y values")

# Line plot
plot(x, y, type = "l", main = "Line Plot", col = "blue")

# Bar plot
barplot(y, names.arg = x, main = "Bar Plot", col = "lightblue")

# Boxplot
boxplot(y, main = "Box Plot", col = "lightgreen")

title: Working with Lists and Apply Functions
code:
# Create a list
my_list <- list(
  numbers = 1:5,
  letters = c("a", "b", "c"),
  matrix = matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
)

# Access list elements
print(my_list$numbers)
print(my_list[["letters"]])

# Apply functions
numbers <- c(1, 4, 9, 16, 25)
sqrt_numbers <- sapply(numbers, sqrt)
print(sqrt_numbers)

# lapply example
result <- lapply(1:3, function(x) x^2)
print(result)
